title: Quickshell socket client: broadcast Lagged error permanently kills the client's writer task
description:
In RustApp/src/quickshell.rs handle_client(), the writer task loop is 'while let Ok(line) = rx.recv().await'. The broadcast channel has capacity 64 and t:"wave" is broadcast on every audio chunk, so a slow or stale client makes rx.recv() return Err(RecvError::Lagged). The loop then exits FOREVER: that client silently stops receiving all state/config/wave/log updates until the user manually reconnects the widget.

Fix sketch: loop { match rx.recv().await { Ok(line) => {...}, Err(broadcast::error::RecvError::Lagged(n)) => { warn; continue; }, Err(_) => break } }
notes: Found in code review of the feat/quickshell-ui branch (2025 review session). No fix applied yet.

title: Widget/standalone GUI never (re)connects to the daemon: one-shot Socket.connected binding
description:
Panel.qml and AndroidMic.qml created the Quickshell Socket with a one-shot binding 'connected: true' / 'connected: !root.mock'. Quickshell's Socket does not auto-retry: if the bar loads before the daemon binds /run/user/1000/android-mic.qsock (boot race: both start around graphical-session.target), or the daemon restarts while the panel is open, connected drops to false forever. Symptom: bar shows dead DISCONNECTED state although the daemon is healthy.

Fix: explicit connect on Component.onCompleted + a 2s repeating reconnect Timer that sets connected = true whenever the socket is down (guarded by !root.mock). Applied to both omarchy/Panel.qml and AndroidMic.qml, synced to the installed plugin via install-omarchy.sh's target (~/.config/omarchy/plugins/androidmic.quickshell) and shell restarted.
notes: Reported live on 2026-08-28: 'daemon does not come live' after reboot; daemon was verified healthy via socket snapshot; root cause was the widget-side one-shot connect.

title: Waveform (live feed) in Quickshell widget stays empty: streamer skips mono mixdown when no cosmic main window exists
description:
## Symptom

The Omarchy bar widget (and the standalone dialogs) show an empty field below the connect/disconnect button: the waveform Canvas (`Panel.qml` ~line 207 — `Rectangle` + `Canvas` + 32 ms repaint `Timer` running while `root.streaming`). In the original cosmic app a live waveform is fed from the input stream; in `--quickshell` mode it never moves. In mock mode it *does* animate, which proves the QML render path (socket → `accumulateWave()` → `root.wave` → `onPaint: drawWave()`) is correct.

## Causal chain (all steps verified against branch `feat/quickshell-ui`)

1. **Headless mode never creates a cosmic window.**
   - `RustApp/src/ui/app.rs:52` — `.no_main_window(true)`
   - `RustApp/src/ui/app.rs:672` — `main_window: None`
   - `RustApp/src/ui/app.rs:705` — `open_main_window()` is only pushed when `!quickshell_mode`
   - ⇒ `AppState.main_window` is `None` for the daemon's whole lifetime.

2. **Every streamer start derives window-visibility from that `None`.**
   - `RustApp/src/ui/app.rs:175` — `update_audio_stream()`: `is_window_visible: self.main_window.is_some()`
   - `RustApp/src/ui/app.rs:258` — `connect()`: `is_window_visible: self.main_window.is_some()`
   - ⇒ `is_window_visible` is **always `false`** in `--quickshell` mode.

3. **The audio processor computes the display waveform ONLY when the window is visible.**
   - `RustApp/src/audio/process.rs:226–244` (return at 244):
     ```rust
     let buffer_mono = if self.is_window_visible {
         Some(/* mono-channel mixdown of the received packet */)
     } else {
         None
     };
     Ok(buffer_mono)
     ```
   - This is an **upstream optimization**: skip the mono mixdown when no cosmic GUI window exists to paint it into. The Quickshell widget is **not** the cosmic window, so the optimization starves it.

4. **Streamers only emit wave messages when the processor returned `Some`.**
   - `RustApp/src/streamer/tcp_streamer.rs:145`, `udp_streamer.rs:119`, `usb_streamer.rs:239`:
     ```rust
     Ok(Some(buffer)) => StreamerMsg::UpdateAudioWave { data: ... }
     _                => Ok(None)   // <- taken when is_window_visible == false
     ```

5. **The socket bridge broadcasts on that message** (app.rs `StreamerMsg::UpdateAudioWave` handler: `broadcast({"t":"wave",...})`). Since (4) never fires, no `t:"wave"` is ever sent; the daemon side of the new pipeline stays silent. QML accumulates nothing; the Canvas paints an empty curve.

**Conclusion:** not a QML bug, not a socket bug. Waveform computation is gated on an upstream GUI-visibility flag that headless mode can never satisfy.

## Fix options

### Option A — client-count-gated flag (precise; saves CPU when no widget is open)
Track connected Quickshell clients in `RustApp/src/quickshell.rs` (increment in `handle_client`, decrement on disconnect) via an `AtomicUsize`; expose `client_count()`. At app.rs:175/258 pass:
```rust
is_window_visible: self.main_window.is_some() || crate::quickshell::client_count() > 0
```
- **Pro:** zero waveform cost while no widget is open.
- **Con:** the flag is only read when the streamer (re)starts, so a client that connects **mid-stream** stays waveless until `update_audio_stream()` runs again → must trigger a stream reconfigure when the *first* client attaches (e.g. reuse `SnapshotRequested` or add a `ClientAttached` command).

### Option B — always compute mixdown in quickshell mode (simplest)
Treat the waveform as wanted whenever running headless:
```rust
is_window_visible: self.main_window.is_some() || flags.quickshell   // (or simply `true` on Linux)
```
- **Pro:** one-line-ish change; works regardless of *when* clients attach.
- **Con:** always pays the per-packet mono mixdown even with zero widget clients connected (cost is small: one averaged pass over each packet).

### Option C — semantic rename (cleanest; largest diff)
Rename `is_window_visible` → `wants_waveform` (or `wave_enabled`) through `AudioParams`/`StreamerCommand` (`streamer/mod.rs:40,52,61`; `streamer_runner.rs:44–191`; `audio/process.rs:226`) and set it from `window visible OR quickshell client attached`.
- **Pro:** makes upstream intent explicit; unblocks any future non-cosmic GUI.
- **Con:** touches upstream code paths broadly → larger rebase surface for future upstream merges.

## Mandatory companion work (for any option)

- **Throttle the `t:"wave"` broadcast** (AndroidMic-3dp): enabling the feed broadcasts on *every* audio chunk.
- **Fix the Lagged writer-kill** (AndroidMic-tnd, P0): the wave flood at full rate will trigger it; slow clients would permanently lose updates.
- QML needs **no** change: `Panel.qml` already repaints via the 32 ms Timer and handles `t:"wave"`.

## Regression risk

None expected on non-Linux: `is_window_visible` keeps meaning the real window there. Option A must cfg-gate `client_count()` to read `0` on non-Linux so builds stay warning-free (see AndroidMic-hft).
acceptance_criteria: 1. With the daemon in --quickshell mode and the bar widget connected, pressing connect produces t:"wave" messages on the socket (verifiable by watching the widget waveform animate). 2. Waveform renders in both Panel.qml and InfoWindow.qml. 3. If Option A: no wave broadcast while zero quickshell clients are attached, and wave data starts within ~1s of first client attach (stream reconfigure on first attach works). 4. cargo check clean on Linux, no new warnings. 5. Non-Linux build path unchanged (window-visibility semantics preserved).
notes:
Found while investigating user report: widget shows large empty field below connect/disconnect; original app had live waveform. QML rendering path verified OK; data starvation is Rust-side. No fix applied.
Expanded with precise causal chain (verified file:line references) and three fix options (A: client-count-gated flag; B: always-on in headless; C: semantic rename to wants_waveform) plus mandatory companion work (throttle + Lagged fix).
DECISION NEEDED: which fix option to implement - A (client-count-gated is_window_visible + reconfigure on first client attach), B (always-on mixdown in quickshell mode, simplest), or C (semantic rename is_window_visible -> wants_waveform, cleanest but largest upstream diff). All options require the blocking companions AndroidMic-tnd and AndroidMic-3dp to land first or together. Awaiting owner choice before implementation.

title: apply_config: invalid 'ip' value silently clears configured ip to None (falls back to auto-selected adapter)
description: RustApp/src/ui/app.rs apply_config(), arm "ip": 'c.ip = s.parse::<IpAddr>().ok();'. A malformed IP sent from the GUI sets c.ip to None; ip_or_default() then returns a network-adapter IP that the user never chose, with no error shown. Better: on parse failure keep the old value and log a warning (or surface an error to the widget).
notes: Found in code review of feat/quickshell-ui. No fix applied yet.

title: apply_config: 'port' value silently truncated via 'as u16' (wrap-around for >65535)
description: RustApp/src/ui/app.rs apply_config(), arm "port": 'c.port = n as u16;' truncates any u64 value. Sending 65537 from the QML GUI silently wraps to port 1. Validate with u16::try_from(n).ok() and ignore out-of-range values (and ideally reject in GUI).
notes: Found in code review of feat/quickshell-ui. No fix applied yet.

title: FILE-INVENTORY.md misstates the Cargo.toml diff (claims ksni/libxdo removal; net diff only adds serde_json)
description: FILE-INVENTORY.md section 'RustApp/Cargo.toml' claims the diff removed the ksni/tray-icon crate and the native libxdo link. The net diff vs origin/main shows only '+serde_json = "1"' plus a cosmetic reorder of the windows/not(linux) dependency blocks. tray-icon was already cfg(not(target_os="linux")) upstream; ksni and libxdo never appear in either manifest. Fix the entry so the change statement stays accurate (matters for GPL 'state your changes' requirement).
notes: Found in code review of feat/quickshell-ui. No fix applied yet.

title: Non-audio config keys (theme, auto_connect, start_minimized, connection_mode, ip, port) trigger update_audio_stream() while connected
description: apply_quick_command() calls self.update_audio_stream() after EVERY apply_config(). update_audio_stream() is a no-op when disconnected, but while connected it tears down and rebuilds the running audio output stream for settings that don't affect audio at all (theme, auto_connect, start_minimized, connection_mode, ip, port). Only audio-relevant keys (sample_rate, channel_count, audio_format, denoise*, amplify*, post_effect) should restart the stream.
notes: Found in code review of feat/quickshell-ui. No fix applied yet.

title: Wave broadcast has no throttle: t:"wave" sent on every audio chunk to all clients
description: StreamerMsg::UpdateAudioWave handler in RustApp/src/ui/app.rs broadcasts a JSON wave message to every socket client on every audio chunk, at full stream rate. Combined with the 64-capacity broadcast channel this is what triggers AndroidMic-tnd (Lagged kills the client writer). Consider broadcasting every Nth chunk or on a fixed tick.
notes: Found in code review of feat/quickshell-ui. No fix applied yet.

title: Bar widget: dropdown fields overflow the dialog viewbox (right border not visible)
description:
## Summary

In the Omarchy bar widget (`RustApp/quickshell/omarchy/Panel.qml`), the settings input
(dropdown) fields did not fit inside the rendered dialog viewbox: each field's right
border fell outside the visible panel, so there was no vertical line closing the field
box. The dialog's popup card clipped the overflowing rows at the right edge.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Click the AndroidMic mic icon in the Omarchy bar to open the panel.
2. Look at any "AUDIO FORMAT" / "CONNECTION" setting row (Device, Sample rate, Channels,
   Format, Mode, etc.).
3. The dropdown field extends past the right edge of the dialog; its right border is
   not visible / not aligned within the viewbox.

## Root cause

Two interacting layout defects in `Panel.qml`:

- The settings `Column` was sized to `width: panel.contentWidth` (400), but the
  `KeyboardPanel` card insets its content by the popup padding, so the actual scroll
  viewport is narrower. Rows sized `width: parent.width` therefore overflowed past the
  card's visible right edge.
- The `Column` also carried its own `leftPadding`/`rightPadding` (14) on top of the
  card's inset, pushing every row's right edge even further out of view, so each
  field's right border landed flush against / outside the dialog rim.

## Fix

- Bind the settings `Column` (and `Flickable.contentWidth`) to `scroll.width`, the real
  scroll viewport, instead of `panel.contentWidth`.
- Remove the `Column`'s own horizontal padding (the card already insets content), while
  keeping vertical padding so rows don't touch the panel edges. Rows now fill the
  viewport fairly and each field's right border is visible inside the dialog.

Dialog width is unchanged; only alignment/overflow was corrected.

## Notes

- QML-only change: `Panel.qml` in `RustApp/quickshell/omarchy/` (and the deployed copy
  under `~/.config/omarchy/plugins/androidmic.quickshell/`). No Rust rebuild needed.
- Because Quickshell caches QML per URL, a **cold shell restart** (`omarchy-restart-shell`)
  is required for the fix to actually render; a plugin rescan alone leaves the stale
  cached version running. This caching is what made the bug appear to persist after the
  file was already corrected.
notes: Verified: all dropdown fields are now correctly aligned within the dialog viewbox. Each field's right border is visible and neatly inset inside the panel, and the fields line up in a right-hand column (left edge set by the longest label) with a clean label-to-field gap. Fix is live (commits 489aaae, 4bfc8e2, fef471c) after a cold shell restart. Closing as resolved.

title: Virtual-mic auto-select heuristic may match unrelated hardware devices
description: In AppState::new() the fallback device pick matches names containing 'virtual_mic', 'virtual mic', or starting with 'android'. A hardware device whose name starts with 'Android' (or generically contains 'virtual') would be auto-selected and persisted into config. Consider matching the exact sink name created by RustApp/quickshell/systemd/androidmic-virtual-mic.sh instead.
notes: Found in code review of feat/quickshell-ui. Edge case. No fix applied yet.

title: qs_broadcast_snapshot() call in AppState::new() is a no-op (OUT_TX not yet set)
description: In AppState::new() the #[cfg(linux)] block calls app.qs_broadcast_snapshot() at startup, but the quickshell::subscribe() subscription hasn't run yet, so OUT_TX is not set and broadcast() silently drops. Harmless because clients send SnapshotRequested on connect, but as written it is dead code. Either remove it or make snapshot-on-startup actually work if ever needed.
notes: Found in code review of feat/quickshell-ui. No fix applied yet.

title: systemd unit comment is stale: claims daemon registers a StatusNotifierItem/tray via D-Bus
description: RustApp/quickshell/systemd/androidmic-daemon.service header comment says the unit 'registers a StatusNotifierItem/tray via D-Bus', but the system tray was removed (commit 4e1de47) - the bar widget is the only GUI. Update the comment to describe the headless --quickshell socket daemon.
notes: Found in code review of feat/quickshell-ui. No fix applied yet.

title: Non-Linux builds: unused variable warning for quickshell_mode in AppState::new()
description: In RustApp/src/ui/app.rs AppState::new(), 'let quickshell_mode = false;' is cfg'd in for non-Linux but only consumed inside a #[cfg(target_os = "linux")] arm of the single_instance closure, so Windows builds emit an unused-variable warning. Add 'let _ = quickshell_mode;' or cfg the binding accordingly.
notes: Found in code review of feat/quickshell-ui. No fix applied yet.

title: add_log() always broadcasts level 'info', even for error logs
description: RustApp/src/ui/app.rs add_log() broadcasts {"t":"log","level":"info",...} unconditionally, including messages arriving via StreamerMsg::Error. Cosmetic: the GUI can't style error lines. Consider threading the level through or heuristically flagging errors.
notes: Found in code review of feat/quickshell-ui. No fix applied yet.

title: Startup auto-select persists device_id into user config as a side effect of first launch
description: Behavior note from review: AppState::new() writes the auto-selected (virtual-mic or default) device_id back into the user's config file on startup when device_id is empty. This deviates from upstream behavior (config only changes when the user acts). Intentional per commit 358d871, but worth documenting in README-OMARCHY or adding a config key to opt out, so users aren't surprised their config file changed.
notes: Found in code review of feat/quickshell-ui. Intentional design; no fix required.
